note: Re-judged 2026-11-10 (independent auditor, not the author of 31f16fc038 or its follow-up) after three tagged units joined the row in rfc7296_unprotected_handshake_test.go. RFC 7296 Section 2.4, read in rfc/full/rfc7296.txt: "Since IKE is designed to operate in spite of DoS attacks from the network, an endpoint MUST NOT conclude that the other endpoint has failed based on any routing information (e.g., ICMP messages) or IKE messages that arrive without cryptographic protection (e.g., Notify messages complaining about unknown SPIs)." The earlier enforced verdict was a half-truth: the obligation binds every endpoint, and the initiator role does not meet it. The row now carries {partial}. Tested: "conclude that the other endpoint has failed based on any routing information (e.g., ICMP messages) or IKE messages that arrive without cryptographic protection". Gap: "an endpoint". Producer: internal/component/ike/engine/fsm.go::handleAuthResponse sets StateDead when the first IKE_AUTH response fails decryptSKPayload (only the RFC 4739 second exchange returns first), and handleEAPResponse in fsm.go sets StateDead on every EAP-round decrypt failure; journal unprotected-message-changes-sa-state 2026-09-29, owned by spec-single-owner-lifecycle. Tested scope, judged unit by unit. ICMP (unchanged since 2026-10-12): TestRFC7296ICMPUnreachableDoesNotFailTheSA and TestRFC7296ICMPFromThePeerWhileWaitingFailsNothing drive a real queued Port Unreachable through the transport error queue and assert the SA stays Established, the probe stays outstanding with no sa-failed answer, nothing reaches Refusals, and an authenticated answer still settles it. Established SA (unchanged): TestRteUnownedEstablishedSATrustsNothing refuses cleartext Delete and CREATE_CHILD_SA and still ends the SA on an authenticated Delete. IKE_SA_INIT (unchanged): TestResponderKeepsOldSAOnUnauthenticatedInit and TestResponderAcceptsReinitAfterStaleSA. New responder-handshake units, read in full: TestResponderAuthSurvivesUnprotectedIKEAuth and TestResponderEAPSurvivesUnprotectedIKEAuth deliver through handleInbound two forgeries at the real request's Message ID, a bare 28-octet header with no SK payload and the genuine sealed request with its last octet (ICV or AEAD tag) flipped, so each isolates a failed cryptographic check from every other rule; they assert the exact state (StateSAInitReceived, StateEAPInProgress), the unchanged next Message ID on the EAP path, exactly two counts under handshake-unauthenticated, no datagram sent, and then the held-back genuine request drives both sides to Established. Against a handler that set StateDead on any decrypt error (the defect) each goes red on the state assertion. TestResponderEAPEndsOnAuthenticatedMalformedRound is the counterweight a vacuous ignore-every-error handler would fail: a round sealed under the initiator's own keys whose inner chain does not parse ends the handshake (StateDead) and moves the counter by zero, so the protected/unprotected boundary is pinned from both sides. Revert records on discardUnauthenticatedHandshakeRequest exist for all three; the follow-up edit to that function is comment-only, so its behavior fingerprint is unchanged. Untagged siblings strengthen the scope without carrying claims: TestResponderSecondAuthRoundDropsUnprotectedRequestQuietly (RFC 4739 second IKE_AUTH, same assertions plus no WARN line), TestResponderSecondAuthRoundEndsOnAuthenticatedMalformedRequest, TestDecryptMarksAuthenticatedPaddingFailureAsInner (a CBC Pad Length wrong under a valid ICV is errInnerParse, a flipped ICV is not) and TestUnprotectedInputDoesNotExtendTheHandshake (forgeries do not refresh CreatedAt, the half-open reaper still ends the handshake). Limit: the responder assertions cover the handshake handlers that call discardUnauthenticatedHandshakeRequest; a new handshake handler would need its own test. Tests not re-run by this judge.
